{"findings": [
  {
    "file": "packages/lib/getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts",
    "line": 20,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "api",
    "title": "UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt/googleChannelId on selected calendars, breaking other callers",
    "body": "The `UserWithCalendars` type now requires every entry of `allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` to include `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`. `getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb` is called from many places besides the updated `connectedCalendars.handler` (e.g. availability/booking flows and event-type handlers) whose user queries select only `externalId`, `integration`, and `eventTypeId` for selected calendars. Those call sites no longer satisfy this type and will fail type-checking (or must be updated to select the extra fields even though they don't need them). The PR only updates `UserRepository.findUnlockedUserForSession`; the other callers were not updated."
  },
  {
    "file": "packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx",
    "line": 42,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "deleteCache mutation does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query",
    "body": "The `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop; unlike `disconnectMutation` right below it, it never invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. After a successful cache deletion the dropdown continues to show the old \"Last updated\" timestamp (because `cacheUpdatedAt` comes from that query) until something else triggers a refetch, so the UI displays stale cache status and continues offering to delete a cache that no longer exists. Add `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` in the mutation's onSettled/onSuccess."
  },
  {
    "file": "packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx",
    "line": 89,
    "severity": "low",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Cache timestamp is always formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale",
    "body": "`new Intl.DateTimeFormat(\"en-US\", ...)` ignores the user's configured locale, so non-English users see US date/time formatting for the cache \"Last updated\" timestamp even though the rest of the app localizes dates. Use the user's locale (e.g. from `useLocale` / navigator.language) or dayjs with the user's locale instead of the hardcoded string."
  },
  {
    "file": "packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.ts",
    "line": 173,
    "severity": "low",
    "category": "data",
    "title": "getCacheStatusByCredentialIds reports expired cache entries as active cache",
    "body": "The groupBy query has no `expiresAt` filter, so rows whose `expiresAt` is in the past (no longer served by `getCachedAvailability`, which filters `expiresAt >= now`) still produce an `updatedAt` value. The UI then shows \"Cache Status / Last updated\" and the delete-cache action for credentials whose cache is effectively dead, which is misleading. Add `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` to the where clause if the intent is to show only live cache."
  },
  {
    "file": "apps/web/package.json",
    "line": 11,
    "severity": "low",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "dev:cron now uses tsx which is not a declared dependency",
    "body": "The script was changed to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, but `tsx` does not appear in dependencies or devDependencies of this package (nor is it added by this PR). `npx` will try to download tsx from the registry on every run in a fresh environment, which fails offline and can pull an unexpected version. Add `tsx` to devDependencies if the script is meant to use it."
  },
  {
    "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts",
    "line": 25,
    "severity": "low",
    "category": "api",
    "title": "Handler throws generic Error instead of TRPCError",
    "body": "When the credential is not found or belongs to another user, the handler throws a plain `Error(\"Credential not found or access denied\")`, which tRPC converts to an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (HTTP 500). Clients cannot distinguish an authorization/not-found failure from a server crash. Throw `new TRPCError({ code: \"NOT_FOUND\" })` (or FORBIDDEN) as other handlers in this codebase do."
  }

findings.title: UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt/googleChannelId on selected calendars, breaking other callers
findings.body: The `UserWithCalendars` type now requires every entry of `allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` to include `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`. `getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb` is called from many places besides the updated `connectedCalendars.handler` (e.g. availability/booking flows and event-type handlers) whose user queries select only `externalId`, `integration`, and `eventTypeId` for selected calendars. Those call sites no longer satisfy this type and will fail type-checking (or must be updated to select the extra fields even though they don't need them). The PR only updates `UserRepository.findUnlockedUserForSession`; the other callers were not updated.

findings.title: deleteCache mutation does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query
findings.body: The `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop; unlike `disconnectMutation` right below it, it never invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. After a successful cache deletion the dropdown continues to show the old "Last updated" timestamp (because `cacheUpdatedAt` comes from that query) until something else triggers a refetch, so the UI displays stale cache status and continues offering to delete a cache that no longer exists. Add `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` in the mutation's onSettled/onSuccess.

findings.title: Cache timestamp is always formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale
findings.body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` ignores the user's configured locale, so non-English users see US date/time formatting for the cache "Last updated" timestamp even though the rest of the app localizes dates. Use the user's locale (e.g. from `useLocale` / navigator.language) or dayjs with the user's locale instead of the hardcoded string.

findings.title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds reports expired cache entries as active cache
findings.body: The groupBy query has no `expiresAt` filter, so rows whose `expiresAt` is in the past (no longer served by `getCachedAvailability`, which filters `expiresAt >= now`) still produce an `updatedAt` value. The UI then shows "Cache Status / Last updated" and the delete-cache action for credentials whose cache is effectively dead, which is misleading. Add `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` to the where clause if the intent is to show only live cache.

findings.title: dev:cron now uses tsx which is not a declared dependency
findings.body: The script was changed to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, but `tsx` does not appear in dependencies or devDependencies of this package (nor is it added by this PR). `npx` will try to download tsx from the registry on every run in a fresh environment, which fails offline and can pull an unexpected version. Add `tsx` to devDependencies if the script is meant to use it.

findings.title: Handler throws generic Error instead of TRPCError
findings.body: When the credential is not found or belongs to another user, the handler throws a plain `Error("Credential not found or access denied")`, which tRPC converts to an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (HTTP 500). Clients cannot distinguish an authorization/not-found failure from a server crash. Throw `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" })` (or FORBIDDEN) as other handlers in this codebase do.
